next_step: Finalize PoC scope + sign ATO questionnaire; run 2-week PoC on dedicated pool
notes:
Account background:
- Founded 2016, omnichannel contact center SaaS; large telco & financial services customers.
- Current stack: Genesys routing, home-grown CRM, events forwarded to Kafka.
- Handling ~15M inbound user messages / month; peak concurrent chats ~10k during promos.

Why Redwood is a fit:
- Need predictable unit economics for chat deflection and agent assist at high volume. very cost-sensitive.
- Want unified runtime across hosted + VPC for pilot -> prod.
- Need routing/fallbacks during spikes (auto-fallback to smaller quantized model or cached replies).

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria (from Alex Park, VP Product):
- Deflection target: 35-45% of web chat volume within 90 days.
- p95 latency goal for agent-assist: <= 300ms; for deflection messages acceptable up to 600ms if throughput preserved.
- Cost target: equivalent to < $0.0006 per user-message at production volumes (includes batching gains).
- Peak reliability: maintain degraded service (cached replies / model-fallback) during regional outages - no full drop to synchronous human routing.
- Security: SSO (SAML), audit logs retention 2y, KMS for key control, data residency for EU customers.

Model & infra preferences / constraints:
- Preference for quantized open models (Llama-3 q8_0 or equivalent) for deflection; smaller local model for failover.
- Need KV/prefix caching for repetitive flows (billing questions, password resets).
- Expect to use batching during off-peak windows for lower-cost downstream tasks (summaries, embeddings).
- Routing policy: region-aware first, then model-tier fallback (hosted -> dedicated -> private small model).

PoC plan (agreed on 2026-02-24 call):
- 2-week technical PoC on dedicated pool (staging), ingest 7 days of anonymized transcripts.
- Goals: validate deflection rate with Redwood Optimize recommendations + measure unit cost per 100k messages.
- Deliverables: latency/cost breakdown dashboard, suggested batching/quant settings, 1 canary route configured.
- Success metric: >30% automated deflection in controlled traffic test and cost projection within target.

Recent activity timeline:
- 2026-01-12: Intro call (Fireflies ff-20260112-349). initial discovery, owner: Maya.
- 2026-01-26: Security kickoff; CISO sent questionnaire (drive:/security/conversepilot-scc-review.docx).
- 2026-02-10: Demo of hosted API + streaming, engineer follow-up (gt-17c9b2d).
- 2026-02-24: PoC scope agreed, Redwood to provide pricing model and dedicated pool sizing (Fireflies ff-20260224-881).
- 2026-03-05: Security call with infra team; asked for SOC2 type II evidence and KMS integration notes (ticket SEC-1298).

Quotes / call notes:
- "We can’t afford to double our costs for a 5% improvement in CSAT — need clear unit economics." — Alex Park
- SE note: "Prefer canary routes + auto-fallback to q4 quantized variant when latency spikes."

Integration notes / tech debt:
- Must integrate Redwood SDK with existing Kafka event bus (delays 50-200ms currently).
- Genesys connector: require webhook mapping and agent UI plugin for inline suggestions.
- Data transformation: transcript normalization required before caching to avoid PII leakage.

Open questions for Redwood team:
- Which quantization profiles give the best tradeoff for our short-context chat (avg 140 tokens)?
- Can Redwood Optimize provide automated autoscaling rules tuned for promo-day spikes?
- Pricing ask: scenario-based pricing for 15M msg/mo with 40% deflection vs current human-handled baseline.

Next steps (short):
- Send ATO questionnaire + SOC2 artifacts (Maya) — due 2026-03-12.
- Redwood to provision dedicated PoC pool + sample config (Ethan) — target 2026-03-18.
- Security team to complete review; if green, schedule PoC kickoff 2026-03-22.
public_notes_summary: High-volume contact center looking for cost-optimized chat deflection + reliable fallbacks. Short PoC planned to validate batch/caching/quantization and unit economics.
